title: Subpoena Desk Note — First Hearing Lead for Pending Subpoena Requests, Unemployment Insurance Appeals
content:
Subpoena requests that stand received and not yet decided are counted when an appeal's first hearing is set under Unemployment Insurance Appeals.

**Rule.** The first-setting subpoena lead is the two-subpoena lead days when two or more subpoena requests on the appeal stand received and not yet decided, the one-subpoena lead days when exactly one does, and zero days when none does. The first hearing date found from the first-setting clock and the first-setting target is moved later by this lead before the notice minimum and the weekend rule are applied.

| Subpoena requests on the appeal standing received and not yet decided | First-setting subpoena lead |
|---|---|
| two or more | 10 calendar days |
| exactly one | 7 calendar days |
| none | 0 days |

## What is counted

- Subpoena requests recorded on this appeal whose status is *received* — that is, not yet decided.
- A subpoena request already granted, or already denied, is decided and is not counted.
- Requests of every party on the appeal count alike.

## Cases (hypothetical)

| Subpoena requests on the appeal | Counted | Lead |
|---|---|---|
| one received, one granted | 1 | 7 days |
| two received | 2 | 10 days |
| three received | 3 | 10 days |
| one granted, one denied | 0 | 0 days |

*Illustration:* with two requests received and undecided, a first hearing date found from the clock and the target of Thursday 7 May 2026 moves 10 days later, to Sunday 17 May, before the notice minimum and the weekend rule are applied.
